sections.offseason: **Atlanta rebuilt the top of the building.** Kevin Stefanski replaced Raheem Morris as head coach, Ian Cunningham took over as GM, and Matt Ryan came back as President of Football Operations, with Tommy Rees calling offense and Jeff Ulbrich running the defense. The Falcons added Tua Tagovailoa as insurance behind Michael Penix Jr., drafted CB Avieon Terrell, WR Zachariah Branch and LB Kendal Daniels, and unveiled new uniforms. **Green Bay's offseason was defined by subtraction.** Jonathan Gannon replaced Jeff Hafley as defensive coordinator, center Elgton Jenkins left for Cleveland, and Micah Parsons is still rehabbing the ACL and meniscus he tore last December with a mid-October target. Josh Jacobs has not played a snap, opening the year on the Commissioner's Exempt List after a domestic battery case in Wisconsin, which pushed Green Bay to trade a sixth-rounder to Pittsburgh for Kaleb Johnson on August 30.
sections.matchup: **Two of the least efficient offenses in football meet on three days' rest.** Atlanta carries a league-worst -53.1 offensive EPA through two weeks, the worst two-game mark since the 2006 Raiders, a league-high seven giveaways, and the distinction of being the only team that has not run a single red-zone play. Green Bay is not much healthier on that side: 31st in rushing EPA, a league-low 19% third-down conversion rate (4 of 21), and 45.8% of its drives failing to produce a first down. The Packers are throwing at the second-highest rate in the league (66.7%) because the ground game has produced just 129 yards on 39 carries, and Jordan Love's splits are brutal when the pocket breaks - 33.3% completions and a 42.8 rating under pressure against 63.6% and a 118.4 rating when clean. That matters because Atlanta is third in the NFL in pressure rate (43.4%) while blitzing just 18.5% of the time (29th), and it is facing a Packers line that lost RT Zach Bako-Bewele to a torn patellar tendon. **The counterweight is Green Bay's defense**, which is second in yards per play allowed (3.9), holds RBs to a league-low 2.8 yards per carry, and gave up only 3.6 yards per pass play on early downs.
sections.injuries: **Atlanta got its quarterback back and lost its best corner.** Michael Penix Jr. (knee) practiced in full Monday and Tuesday and was named the Week 3 starter, his first start since a partially torn ACL ended his 2025 in November, with Cooper Rush having started the first two losses. A.J. Terrell Jr. went on injured reserve Tuesday with a groin injury and cannot return until Week 7, pushing C.J. Henderson opposite Mike Hughes, while DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) has not practiced; Tua Tagovailoa (oblique), Brian Robinson Jr. (ankle) and Jawaan Taylor (rib) all upgraded to full. **Green Bay's list is longer and uglier.** Jayden Reed (back, carted off in New York) did not participate either day and RT Zach Bako-Bewele is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, leaving a line where Aaron Banks (knee/toe) missed Monday and Donovan Jennings (hand) and Anthony Belton (elbow) are limited. Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion) and Edgerrin Cooper (shoulder) were limited both days on defense, while Josh Jacobs (Commissioner's Exempt List) and Micah Parsons (ACL, targeting mid-October) remain unavailable entirely.
sections.oddsNotes: **The market has moved toward Atlanta since it opened.** Green Bay opened -7 (and briefly -7.5 at some shops) with a 46.5 total; DraftKings now shows GB -6 with the total bet down to 44.5 and the moneyline at ATL +235 / GB -290. FanDuel is a half-point longer at -6.5 with +220 / -270, and earlier SI-quoted numbers had -7 / -325 / +260, so the steam has been on the Falcons' side and the under. De-vigged, that is roughly a 71% Green Bay win probability and team totals near 25.25 for the Packers and 19.25 for Atlanta. **Model and public opinion are split**: Dimers projects Packers 25, Falcons 17 with a 74.4% GB win probability, while Covers leaned Atlanta +7.5 and NBC's Vaughn Dalzell took the Falcons +6.5, citing Green Bay's line injuries. The under has cashed in both Atlanta games and both teams are 0-2 against the spread.

Green Bay's board is flat and cheap - Christian Watson +125, MarShawn Lloyd +165, Matthew Golden +175, Tucker Kraft +180 and Kaleb Johnson +180 - which is what happens when a team throws on 66.7% of snaps and runs a true three-man backfield committee. **Watson is the only Packer who has actually finished drives**, with three of Green Bay's four passing touchdowns, including two in Week 1 against Minnesota. Tucker Kraft's usage exploded once Reed went down: 98.3% of snaps and an 84.4% route rate in Week 2, and Atlanta plays single-high on 64.6% of snaps, which is the look that feeds seam tight ends. The Falcons side is capped by the fact that they have literally never snapped the ball inside the 20 this year, so every Atlanta number other than Robinson should be treated as a projection, not a trend.

sections.offseason:
**Buffalo reset the sideline and got an immediate return.** Sean McDermott was fired after the playoff loss to Denver and Joe Brady was promoted from coordinator to head coach, and the Bills are 2-0 with 36+ points in both games. They added **DJ Moore** by trade from Chicago, **Bradley Chubb** and **C.J. Gardner-Johnson** on defense, and opened the new Highmark Stadium with a 41-31 win over Detroit after a 36-31 win at Houston.
- Josh Allen has 582 pass yards, 5 pass TDs, 4 rush TDs and zero turnovers, and is the **+250 MVP favorite**.
- Buffalo leads the league at 7.1 yards per play and 38.5 points per game, but has allowed 31 points in each game.
**Los Angeles hired the offense it wanted and it has not shown up yet.** Jim Harbaugh brought in **Mike McDaniel** as offensive coordinator to unlock Justin Herbert, and instead the Chargers are 0-2 with identical 26-14 home losses to Arizona and Las Vegas. Herbert is 32-of-54 for 401 yards with 2 TDs and 3 INTs, the offense sits 28th in points per drive at 1.22, and Los Angeles has run only 27% of its snaps in opponent territory, worst in the NFL.
sections.matchup:
**Buffalo's run game and Allen's legs meet the one thing Los Angeles does well.** The Chargers are allowing just 86.5 rush yards per game, rank around 8th in EPA per rush allowed, and bottled up Ashton Jeanty in Week 2, so **James Cook III** (34 carries, 192 yards) may have to grind. That matters less at the goal line, where Allen is essentially a designed short-yardage runner and has already scored from one and two yards out this season.
- Buffalo has hit 20+ yard runs four times, tied for most in the NFL, and leads the league in play-action success at 62%.
- The Bills pressured the quarterback 14 times in Week 2, most in the NFL, and Greg Rousseau already has 4 sacks.
**Los Angeles has to throw into the one area Buffalo is soft.** The Bills are surrendering 300.5 pass yards and 31 points per game with zero interceptions, which is the lone path for a Chargers offense that has to play from behind. With both blocking tight ends gone, expect heavy 11 personnel, quick game over the middle, and concentrated targets to **Ladd McConkey** and check-downs to **Omarion Hampton**, who draws a Bills front that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points to running backs.
sections.injuries:
**The Chargers are the far more compromised team.** Tight ends **David Njoku** (fibula) and **Charlie Kolar** (forearm) are both on injured reserve and out at least four weeks, leaving **Oronde Gadsden** as the only tight end on the active roster. Starting left guard Kayode Awosika and starting defensive tackle **Dalvin Tomlinson** (hamstring, doubtful) are both expected to miss time per Jim Harbaugh, and All-Pro safety **Derwin James Jr.** will play in a protective cast on a broken thumb.
- Also questionable for LAC: CB **Elijah Molden** (hamstring), CB **Deane Leonard** (abdomen), OT **Trey Pipkins III** (knee).
- **Ladd McConkey** played through a rib issue in Week 2 and is not on the report.
**Buffalo's list is shorter but touches the passing game.** WR **DJ Moore** is questionable with an AC joint sprain and has been called day-to-day, RB **Ty Johnson** (hamstring) has missed two straight, and DT **Ed Oliver** (hip spasms) and DT **T.J. Sanders** (knee) are questionable. WR Tyrell Shavers is out for the year after ACL surgery.

**Both teams sit 1-1 with wildly different Week 1 and Week 2 tape.** Carolina opened by losing a 59-37 track meet to Chicago, then flipped the script with a 34-3 rout at Atlanta in which the defence forced five turnovers. Bryce Young is 46-of-73 for 648 yards with six touchdowns and one interception, and Carolina leads the league with a 72.4% neutral-script dropback rate.
- **Cleveland reset under Todd Monken**, opening with a 34-10 loss at Jacksonville before a 23-19 win at Tampa Bay in which Deshaun Watson went 24-of-30 for 238 yards and two scores.
- **Roster churn matters here**: the Browns traded Myles Garrett to the Rams and brought back Jared Verse, while rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have leapfrogged Jerry Jeudy.
- Sunday is Cleveland's home opener; Carolina has not beaten the Browns since 2014.
sections.matchup:
**The league's second-ranked scoring offence against a Cleveland defence that has been schematically volatile.** Carolina is averaging 35.5 points and 6.7 yards per play and has run a league-high 31 red-zone plays through two weeks. The counterweight is coverage: Cleveland played man on a league-high 62.9% of snaps in Week 2 after 21.4% in Week 1, and Bryce Young's splits are stark, a 133.4 rating against zone versus 67.1 against man.
- **Cleveland's offence is the drag.** The Browns are 24th at 16.5 points a game, run only 52 plays a game and have the league's worst rushing efficiency, with Quinshon Judkins at 54 yards on 24 carries.
- **Carolina's defence is the counter-argument to a low number**, ranking 28th at 31.0 points and 6.1 yards per play allowed.
- Watson's profile is fragile: 68.1% of his passing yardage has come after the catch and he has absorbed seven sacks.
sections.injuries:
**Carolina's offensive line and edge rotation are the biggest concerns.** Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu remains on PUP, right tackle Taylor Moton is on the non-football injury list and Brady Christensen is on IR, leaving a patched front against Jared Verse and Mason Graham. Edge Nic Scourton is out for the year and Tershawn Wharton is on PUP.
- **Backfield note**: Jonathon Brooks is doubtful with a groin strain and Trevor Etienne is on IR, funnelling work to Chuba Hubbard.
- Rookie receiver Chris Brazzell II is on IR; Xavier Legette has been managed with a hamstring.
- **Cleveland** is without Dylan Sampson (IR), Dillon Gabriel (IR), Alex Wright (IR) and Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah (PUP), with Tyson Campbell and Teven Jenkins questionable.

sections.offseason:
**Aaron Glenn returns to Ford Field**, where he spent four seasons as Detroit's defensive coordinator before taking the Jets job; he is in year two with GM Darren Mougey and new OC Frank Reich.
- Geno Smith is the Jets' quarterback, with Breece Hall extended and rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. added alongside Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor.
- Detroit signed Isiah Pacheco to back up Jahmyr Gibbs, but Pacheco had back surgery and landed on IR, leaving Gibbs with an enormous share behind Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki.
- Both clubs enter **1-1**: the Jets beat Tennessee 23-10 and lost 20-17 in overtime to Green Bay; the Lions edged New Orleans 31-30 in OT and lost 41-31 in Buffalo.
sections.matchup:
**The league's best defense so far against one of its best offenses, and the league's worst defense against a limited one.** New York leads the NFL in total defense at 197 yards per game, ranks second against the pass and the run, third in yards per play at 4.0, and first in time-of-possession differential.
- Detroit's offense still averages 362 yards and 31.0 points, but Gibbs was held to 52 yards on 16 carries in Buffalo.
- Going the other way, Detroit has surrendered 917 yards and 71 points in two games, and 51 points in second halves alone.
- Buffalo attacked the middle of that defense with **both tight ends scoring**, which reads through to Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq.
- The counterweight is that the Jets managed only 285 yards and 17 points against Green Bay, and Hall averaged 1.8 yards a carry.
sections.injuries:
**Detroit's secondary is the story.** Safeties Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) are both on reserve and not eligible until Week 5; Avonte Maddox and Rock Ya-Sin both left the Buffalo game hurt, and D.J. Reed has been limited with a foot issue.
- Up front, OL Christian Mahogany (hip) and T Blake Miller (knee) have been unavailable, and Isiah Pacheco (back surgery) is out long term.
- For the Jets, safety **Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) has been ruled out** for two to three weeks; WRs Tim Patrick (groin) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) are on reserve.
- Edge Joseph Ossai is close to returning; confirm final Friday designations before betting sides or props.

Both teams walk in at **0-2**, and both got there against the AFC's heavyweights. Houston lost a Week 1 shootout to Buffalo **36-31**, then was shut down in Cincinnati **20-6**, held to 60 rushing yards and 5-of-17 on third down with no touchdowns. Indianapolis was blown out by Baltimore **41-23** in Week 1 and then pushed Kansas City to overtime before losing **33-30**.
- **Houston's identity is the defence**, not the offence; the offence has scored 6 points in the last 8 quarters.
- **Indianapolis' identity is Jonathan Taylor**, who has three rushing touchdowns in two games and went for 132 scrimmage yards and two scores at Arrowhead.
- Daniel Jones has been functional and occasionally explosive, but the Colts have leaned on Taylor to finish drives.
sections.matchup:
This is the league's **worst defence against a broken offence**. Indianapolis is last in the NFL in points allowed (**37.0 a game**), yards allowed (**514.5**) and pass yards allowed, is surrendering **5.4 yards per carry**, and is giving up a touchdown on **67% of opponent red-zone trips**. The Colts' own red-zone offence is the mirror image at roughly **84%**, with Taylor taking the goal-line work and Tyler Warren the short-area targets.
- **Houston should be able to move the ball** — Stroud is averaging 313.5 passing yards and Indy has allowed a 108.4 opposing passer rating — but finishing drives without Collins is the open question.
- **Houston's front is the best unit on the field** and has generated consistent pressure against a Colts line that gave up interior push in both losses.
- Houston has won the last five meetings, **all by eight points or fewer**, so the 2.5 is grounded in series history rather than form.
sections.injuries:
**Both offences are missing their number one receiver.** Alec Pierce aggravated a surgically repaired heel and has been reported out for Week 3 and likely several weeks beyond; Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell absorb his snaps. Nico Collins (grade 1 hamstring) missed Week 2 and is widely expected to miss this one, carrying a questionable tag.
- Houston is also without **Jayden Higgins (IR)** and **Tank Dell (IR-R)**, leaving Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel as the receiver room.
- Other Texans questionable: **Jake Hummel, Ed Ingram, Jadeveon Clowney**.
- Other Colts questionable: **DJ Giddens, Ashton Dulin, Michael Clemons, Charvarius Ward**.

**Miami tore the thing down to the studs.** Tua Tagovailoa was released in March for an NFL-record $99 million dead cap hit, Mike McDaniel was replaced by ex-Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley, and Jaylen Waddle was traded to Denver. Malik Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million deal to reunite with Hafley and the Green Bay staff, giving Miami a dual-threat starter but almost no proven receiving around him. The result through two weeks is a skill group led by rookie-tier names: Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell and Greg Dulcich.
- **Kansas City went the other direction.** After missing the playoffs and ranking 25th in rushing, the Chiefs signed Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $45 million deal and rebuilt a young defense around rookies and second-year players.
- Patrick Mahomes entered the season recovering from a torn ACL, which was part of the rationale for buying a true workhorse back.
sections.matchup:
**Miami has not recorded a single sack through two games.** Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy were both kept completely clean, which is the worst possible profile to bring into a Mahomes game. Kansas City is 6-for-10 scoring touchdowns in the red zone while Miami's defense has surrendered touchdowns on **8 of 9** opponent red-zone trips, including 5-for-5 to San Francisco.
- **Kansas City passes at the goal line.** Their short scores have gone to Xavier Worthy (1 yd), Jalen Royals (1 yd) and Kenneth Walker III (2 yd receiving) through the air; Walker's only rushing touchdown was a 60-yard run. That matters for pricing Walker's touchdown equity.
- **Walker is the engine anyway** at 47 carries for 290 yards plus 16 targets, and Miami has allowed 225 rushing yards on 64 carries. Travis Kelce leads Kansas City with 16 targets and Rashee Rice has eight.
- **Miami's offense is broken in the scoring zone** at 1-for-5 in the red zone with two offensive touchdowns all year: a Willis 14-yard scramble and a 77-yard catch-and-run by depth receiver Ryan Miller. Willis has been sacked nine times behind a leaky line, and Kansas City is allowing just 170.5 passing yards and 260.5 total yards per game while holding the ball 33:42 and 37:00.
sections.injuries:
**Miami's biggest concern is Caleb Douglas (ankle, questionable)**, who leads the team in receiving yards and played 51 of 59 snaps in Week 2 before exiting. Edge rusher Chop Robinson is questionable with a concussion and Robert Beal Jr. is questionable with a hamstring, which is grim for a pass rush already at zero sacks. Jaylen Wright is questionable with a neck issue, which pushed Ollie Gordon II from 4 to 11 snaps in Week 2; Ronnie Harrison Jr. is on injured reserve.
- **Kansas City is comparatively healthy on offense.** Mahomes has been a full practice participant, and Rashee Rice has practiced fully. Omarr Norman-Lott is out for the year with a torn ACL, and Cooper McDonald, Jimmy Holiday, Jeff Caldwell and Matt Waletzko are on IR.
- Chris Jones (calf) and Chamarri Conner have carried questionable or out designations in at least one report; confirm the Friday/Saturday status before playing any Chiefs defensive derivative.

sections.offseason:
**Two brand-new coaching staffs meet here, and the Giants premise checks out.** John Harbaugh was hired on 20 January 2026 as the 21st head coach in Giants history after 18 seasons in Baltimore, with Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator and Dennard Wilson running the defense. New York rebuilt around Harbaugh's Baltimore tastes, importing TE Isaiah Likely, LB Tremaine Edmunds, WR Darnell Mooney and WR Odell Beckham Jr., while trading DT Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati for the 10th pick, spent on OT Francis Mauigoa.
- Tennessee reset too: **Robert Saleh** is in year one as head coach, with **Brian Daboll** as offensive coordinator and Gus Bradley on defense.
- Daboll's arrival pulled two ex-Giants with him: **Wan'Dale Robinson** and **Daniel Bellinger** are both on Tennessee's roster, which is the sharpest sub-plot in the game.
- Tennessee's draft added WR Carnell Tate in Round 1 and DE Keldric Faulk in Round 2 around Cam Ward and Jeffery Simmons, after back-to-back 3-14 seasons.
sections.matchup:
**Two of the league's least productive offenses, and the Week 2 framing is accurate but incomplete.** The Giants did get beaten badly by the Rams on Monday night, 28-6 at SoFi, scoring only two field goals after Jaxson Dart hurt his knee on the opening drive — so the blowout is at least as much a quarterback story as a talent story. New York is 1-1 at 17.0 points and 289.0 yards per game, allowing 24.0 and 367.0; Tennessee is 0-2 at 15.0 points and 256.5 yards, allowing 23.5 and 360.0, with losses of 23-10 to the Jets and 24-20 to the Eagles, both at home.
- **Red-zone and goal-line share:** Cam Skattebo has 30 carries for 117 yards and a touchdown through two games and is the clear goal-line back; Tony Pollard has 21 carries for 99 yards and no scores.
- **End-zone targets:** Isaiah Likely is the Giants' red-area focal point with 13 catches, 111 yards and 2 TDs, and a backup quarterback should push tight-end and back targets higher still.
- Tennessee's front (Jeffery Simmons, John Franklin-Myers, Oluwafemi Oladejo) meets a Giants line missing pieces, while New York's rush — Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Brian Burns — faces Cam Ward on his first road start of the year behind a mid-tier line.
- Tennessee's run defense has been the soft spot at 120.5 rushing yards allowed per game, which is exactly the lane a Winston-led Giants plan wants.
sections.injuries:
**This is the whole game.** Jaxson Dart is listed **doubtful** with a sprained MCL suffered on Monday's opening drive; Ian Rapoport reported negative X-rays with an MRI to follow, and reporting points to a two-to-four-week absence. Jameis Winston is in line to start after going 11-of-27 for 111 yards with an interception and two sacks in relief — a 40.7% completion night.
- **Malik Nabers is questionable** with a shoulder injury; he had 1 catch for 1 yard on 4 targets before leaving, and his status swings the Giants' passing ceiling.
- **LT Andrew Thomas (groin) and Brian Burns (low ankle sprain) are questionable**, with Micah McFadden (neck) also listed and Deonte Banks (calf) already having missed Week 2.
- CB Paulson Adebo and WR Calvin Austin III remain on injured reserve for New York.
- Tennessee is comparatively clean: James Williams Sr. (elbow), Cor'Dale Flott (quadriceps) and Fernando Carmona (shoulder) are questionable, with Milo Eifler and Kendell Brooks on IR.

sections.matchup:
**Cincinnati's run game against Pittsburgh's front seven is the cleanest edge on the board.** The Steelers allow 128 rushing yards per game (eighth-most), a 49.8% rushing success rate (fifth-highest), have missed 17 tackles in run defense and have already given up seven explosive runs. Chase Brown is a genuine bell cow — 25 touches and 20 carries for 80 yards in Week 2, a 72% snap share and a designed goal-line touchdown in Week 1 — while Samaje Perine took just three touches on 40% of snaps.
- **Pittsburgh's passing game is operating in a phone booth.** Aaron Rodgers is one of only four quarterbacks without a completion over 20 air yards, has 51 attempts at or under 10 air yards (fifth-most), and was pressured on 36.8% of dropbacks in Week 2; under pressure he is 10-of-25 for 112 yards with six sacks. That funnels red-zone work to TE Pat Freiermuth (team-leading 9 catches, 78 yards, 1 TD) and to heavy personnel rather than to DK Metcalf, who has caught 8 of 19 targets (42.1%, fifth-lowest).
- **Cincinnati's pass rush is the swing factor.** The Bengals pressured C.J. Stroud on 43.5% of dropbacks with five defenders logging 4+ pressures, rank eighth in pressure rate (39.2%) and seventh in sack rate (8.7%), and have not allowed a passing touchdown all season while holding opponents to a 50% red-zone TD rate on eight trips.
- **The counter is Pittsburgh's pass rush.** The Steelers are fourth in pressure rate (41.5%) with a league-high 13.7% sack rate, and Burrow took five sacks in Week 2 — Cincinnati is compensating by getting the ball out fast (63% of throws inside 2.5 seconds, second in the NFL) with only 29.5% of throws traveling 10+ yards, and leads the league in 12 personnel at 35.2%.
sections.injuries:
**Pittsburgh has the more meaningful absences, and they are concentrated in the secondary and backfield.** CB Joey Porter Jr. is dealing with a back injury and has been reported as seeking a second opinion; he has been carried as out/questionable, leaving newcomer Jamel Dean as CB1 after allowing 7 completions on 9 targets for 89 yards. NBC Sports notes the Steelers secondary ranks 31st in passing yards allowed, which is the softest spot Cincinnati can attack.
- **WR Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is in doubt.** Head coach Mike McCarthy has called it a new foot injury unrelated to his training-camp issue and said he was unsure whether Pittman would play; rookie Germie Bernard took the snaps in Week 2 (8 targets, 35 yards).
- **RB Rico Dowdle (toe) is questionable.** He returned at halftime in Week 2, re-aggravated the toe and was benched. If he is limited, Jaylen Warren's goal-line share rises with Kaleb Johnson as the next man up.
- **Cincinnati is comparatively healthy.** The Bengals came out of Houston without fantasy-relevant injuries; DT B.J. Hill has been listed out/questionable, and Burrow is managing a rib injury he already played through in Week 2. Confirm the Friday/Saturday designations before betting anything Porter-, Pittman- or Dowdle-dependent.
sections.oddsNotes:
**This line has moved hard toward Cincinnati and hard toward the Under.** DraftKings opened the Bengals around -1.5 and the total at 47.5; the game is now CIN -3.5 with a 42.5 total, a five-point drop that reflects both Pittsburgh's offensive collapse and Cincinnati's defensive form. Moneyline is CIN -185 / PIT +154 at DraftKings, with FanDuel a touch longer at -188 / +158 and BetMGM showing -190 / +155 on a 43.5 total.
- **De-vigged, the market gives Cincinnati roughly a 62% win probability**, and the spread and total together imply 23.0 points for the Bengals and 19.5 for the Steelers — RotoWire posts those exact team totals.
- **Models cluster tightly around the number.** Dimers simulates Bengals 23, Steelers 19 with a 64.4% Cincinnati win probability and only a 54.6% cover rate; FanDuel's numberFire has it at 51%; BetMGM's model has the Bengals at 53.4% to win and 51.0% to cover.
- **Trends lean Under.** Pittsburgh is 0-2 to the Over this season and 6-4 to the Under in its last 10; Cincinnati is 7-3 to the Under in its last 10 and 1-1 to the Over in 2026. Covers and NBC Sports both land on Under 42.5, and Covers grades both Bengals -3.5 and the Under as no better than 55% plays.
sections.atdNotes:
**BetMGM has the most complete posted anytime-touchdown board for this game, and it is confirmed across two separate BetMGM write-ups.** Chase Brown is the only player shorter than even money at -125, followed by Jaylen Warren +105, Ja'Marr Chase +115, Tee Higgins +165 and DK Metcalf +180, with the tight ends Mike Gesicki and Pat Freiermuth both at +375.
- **A second book is available on the tight ends and the quarterback.** FanDuel has Freiermuth at +310 and Gesicki at +330, both shorter than BetMGM, and Caesars has Joe Burrow at +1200 versus BetMGM's +575 — so shop the TEs at FanDuel and the quarterback at Caesars.
- **The board's biggest disagreement with the game environment is Jaylen Warren.** A 48.8% implied probability sits on a team projected for 19.5 points that has scored 23 in two games, against a Cincinnati front that held Houston's backs to 18 yards on 14 carries; that is the clearest number to fade even accounting for Dowdle's toe.
- **No price is posted anywhere I could confirm for Germie Bernard or Kaleb Johnson**, both of whom gain snaps if Pittman Jr. and Dowdle sit — those are listed with a null price and flagged to verify.
- All prices are pre-weekend and will move on the Friday and Saturday injury designations, particularly for Porter Jr. and Dowdle.

sections.offseason:
**Seattle arrives as the defending Super Bowl champion but with a rebuilt backfield.** Kenneth Walker III left in free agency for Kansas City, Zach Charbonnet opened the year on reserve/PUP after tearing an ACL in January's divisional round, and the job fell to rookie Jadarian Price alongside Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. The pass game was upgraded instead: Rashid Shaheed joined Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, and Smith-Njigba has been the entire offense so far with 17 catches on 22 targets for 277 yards and four touchdowns. Seattle carries a franchise-record 12-game winning streak into Landover.
- **Washington** paired Stefon Diggs with Terry McLaurin, added tight end Chig Okonkwo, and handed the run game to second-year back Jacory Croskey-Merritt.
- Both clubs changed at quarterback by accident, not design.
sections.matchup:
**This is a bad stylistic draw for a backup-quarterback offense.** Seattle has allowed 17 points in two games, held Arizona to 151 total yards, and leads the league in yards per play allowed at 3.8; Leonard Williams already has two sacks and Ernest Jones IV 21 tackles. Washington's line has been leaky enough that Dallas hung 37 on them, and the Commanders have leaned on 157 rushing yards per game to stay on schedule, with Croskey-Merritt handling the goal-line work and Rachaad White the passing-down role (six catches in Week 2). Going the other way, Washington has surrendered four touchdowns to tight ends in two games - Dallas Goedert twice, Jake Ferguson twice - which is the single clearest seam in this matchup for AJ Barner, who plays 80 percent of Seattle's snaps and took the 1-yard direct-snap score in Arizona.
- **The mirror image:** both touchdowns Seattle has allowed this year also went to tight ends (Eli Raridon, Trey McBride), which lifts Okonkwo, John Bates and Ben Sinnott above their usage.
- Seattle has converted only 33 percent of third downs, so drives may stall into field goals rather than sevens.
sections.injuries:
**Sam Darnold is genuinely in play, but Drew Lock has removed the urgency.** Darnold is listed questionable with the glute/lower-body strain he suffered on Seattle's sixth snap of the season; Mike Macdonald said the plan is for him to practice Wednesday "in some capacity," and he was never placed on short-term IR. Lock has thrown for 422 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions in relief, so Seattle has no pressure to rush the decision. Rookie back Jadarian Price is questionable with the shoulder injury that knocked him out in the fourth quarter at Arizona, with guard Anthony Bradford (knee) also questionable.
- **Washington is the bigger problem:** Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow before halftime against Dallas and is doubtful, and Dan Quinn has already confirmed Marcus Mariota as the Week 3 starter.
- Frankie Luvu (groin), Sam Cosmi (concussion), Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and Nick Cross are all questionable for the Commanders.

**Two 1-1 teams built around opposite strengths.** Jacksonville is in year two under Liam Coen with Grant Udinski calling plays and Anthony Campanile running the defense, and the big offseason add was WR Jakobi Meyers alongside Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington and second-year two-way player Travis Hunter. New England's Mike Vrabel and Josh McDaniels spent heavily on the perimeter and the line, signing WR Romeo Doubs, OG Alijah Vera-Tucker and edge Dre'Mont Jones to support Drake Maye's third season.
- **Jaguars:** beat Cleveland 34-10 at home, then blew a 13-3 lead at Denver and lost 20-13, ending a nine-game regular-season winning streak.
- **Patriots:** lost 13-10 at Seattle, then won 20-3 over Pittsburgh behind a defensive touchdown from Elijah Ponder and 136 rushing yards.
- Jacksonville leads the AFC South; New England is 0-1 on the road and has not scored more than 20 points in a game.
sections.matchup:
**This is a strength-on-weakness game in both directions.** New England's defense is the best unit on the field: it has allowed 3.5 and 5.9 yards per play, just one offensive touchdown in two games, and is 0-for-3 in opponent red-zone touchdown conversions, which is exactly the phase Jacksonville has to win at home. Jacksonville's defense has been the opposite, surrendering 6.1 yards per play (29th) and 191 rushing yards through two weeks, and it gave up two red-zone touchdowns to Denver in the second half.
- **Jaguars offense:** 23.5 points per game, 45.5% on third down, 4-of-4 in red-zone scoring, but Trevor Lawrence was 17-of-29 for 189 yards with an interception and no touchdowns in Denver.
- **Patriots offense:** 15.0 points per game, 32.1% on third down, one offensive passing touchdown all season, and 122.5 rushing yards per game is the only reliable source of yardage.
- **Pass rush:** Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker face a Patriots interior that lost Mike Onwenu; New England has already allowed six sacks and Maye has thrown four interceptions.
- **Pass-game usage:** Parker Washington has 18 targets in two games (12 at Denver) and is Jacksonville's volume hub; TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson have combined for nine targets, and with A.J. Brown out New England leans on Doubs and TE Hunter Henry near the goal line.
sections.injuries:
**New England is the more compromised roster.** WR A.J. Brown is on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain and is out for this game and likely several more, which removes the Patriots' most dangerous red-zone target and pushes Romeo Doubs and Hunter Henry into that role. Right guard Mike Onwenu is also on IR with an ankle injury, a meaningful problem against Jacksonville's edge rushers.
- **Patriots questionable:** CB Carlton Davis III (neck), OT Dametrious Crownover (knee), TE Eli Raridon (thigh), S Dell Pettus (ankle), S Craig Woodson, LB Dre'Mont Jones.
- **Jaguars questionable:** DT DaVon Hamilton (back); DE B.J. Green II, C Sam Mustipher, G Patrick Mekari and DE Zach Durfee are on injured reserve.
- Jacksonville carried WR Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder), WR Jakobi Meyers (thumb) and RB LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) as limited practice participants into Week 2; the Week 3 practice reports post midweek and should be re-checked before betting receiver props.
- TreVeyon Henderson missed Week 1 with an ankle issue and practiced fully before returning to 16 carries in Week 2.

sections.offseason:
**Arizona reset the whole thing.** Jonathan Gannon was fired after 2025, Mike LaFleur took over as head coach and Nathaniel Hackett came in as coordinator after Drew Petzing left for Detroit. Kyler Murray was released on March 11, leaving **Jacoby Brissett** as the starter with rookie Carson Beck (3rd round, Miami) stashed behind him; first-rounder **Jeremiyah Love** out of Notre Dame is the lead back with James Conner unavailable.
- **San Francisco doubled down instead.** The 49ers signed **Mike Evans** to a three-year deal, brought **Deebo Samuel Sr.** back, re-added Dre Greenlaw and patched corner with Nate Hobbs and Jack Jones, while losing Jauan Jennings to Minnesota and Jordan Elliott to Tennessee.
- Second-round rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling had ankle surgery and is out roughly 10 weeks, so the target tree is Evans, Kittle, Samuel and Christian McCaffrey.
- Through two weeks the gap shows: **SF 2-0** (27-7 over the Rams in Melbourne, 35-13 over Miami), **ARI 1-1** (26-14 at the Chargers, then 31-7 at home to Seattle, an eighth straight home loss).
sections.matchup:
**This is a scoring-efficiency mismatch.** San Francisco is averaging **31.0 points (4th)** and 380.5 yards (8th); Arizona sits at **16.5 points (24th)** and 272 yards (26th). Brock Purdy leads the league at **80.4% completions** (45-of-56, 492 yards, 5 TD, 0 INT) and the 49ers rank top-five in red-zone efficiency on both sides of the ball.
- Arizona's passing game is funneled almost entirely through **Trey McBride** (17 catches, 136 yards, 2 TD in two games) and secondarily Michael Wilson; LaFleur has publicly declined to manufacture touches for Marvin Harrison Jr., who has **one catch on four targets** despite 70%+ snaps because he is being used almost exclusively on deep post/go concepts.
- With James Conner out, the goal-line carry share belongs to rookie Jeremiyah Love (20 carries, 70 yards, 1 TD), who is running into a San Francisco front that has been one of the better run-stuff units early.
- On the other side, Evans at 6-5 is the 49ers' designed red-zone answer and Arizona's corner room is banged up, so **end-zone targets should skew to Evans and Kittle** with McCaffrey owning the one- and two-yard work.
- The one soft spot: San Francisco's quick-pressure rate was among the league's worst in Week 1, which is the single path to Brissett having a functional day.
sections.injuries:
**San Francisco is playing through real attrition and still winning.** DT Alfred Collins is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, WR De'Zhaun Stribling is out roughly 10 weeks after ankle surgery, and **Demarcus Robinson and James Thompson Jr. both suffered high-ankle sprains** in Week 2.
- **Mike Evans (hip)** and CB Jack Jones were listed questionable coming out of Week 2, RB Kaelon Black has a groin issue, kicker Eddy Piñeiro missed practice time with illness, and Brandon Aiyuk remains off the active picture. Mykel Williams, Sam Okuayinonu and Christian Kirk all missed Week 2.
- **Arizona's secondary is the bigger problem for this game**: corners **Will Johnson and Max Melton** have both carried questionable tags, and Garrett Williams, Andrew Billings, Josh Fryar, Reggie Virgil and Carson Beck were inactive in Week 2.

**Minnesota reshaped its quarterback room and is 2-0 anyway.** Kyler Murray opened the season as the starter, lasted 11 snaps against Green Bay before a concussion, and Carson Wentz — re-signed as the veteran QB2 with J.J. McCarthy behind him — went 23-of-39 for 276 yards and 3 TDs across the Packers and Bears wins. Jauan Jennings was added to a receiver room already headlined by Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver, while Aaron Jones Sr. remains the lead back. Brian Flores' defense is the identity: 12.5 points allowed per game, eight sacks (tied for most in the NFL) and a league-high 33.6% pressure rate.
- **Tampa Bay's skill group looks different.** Mike Evans is no longer on the roster, leaving Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. as the top two with Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst III rotating up, plus Kenny Gainwell imported to spell Bucky Irving. Todd Bowles is 0-2 and already fielding hot-seat questions in the local press.
sections.matchup:
**This is a strength-on-weakness spot for Minnesota's front.** The Vikings blitz more than any defense in the league and pressure quarterbacks on 33.6% of dropbacks; Baker Mayfield has already absorbed seven sacks in two games and Tampa Bay's pass-success rate (42.4%) is fifth-worst in the NFL. Tampa's answer has been short and safe — repeated screens and swing passes — which shows up in Bucky Irving's 11 catches on 11 targets and Cade Otton's 11 targets through two weeks. Minnesota's own offense is run-leaning and low-volume (147 pass yards and 113 rush yards per game), and its third-down rate is poor, so drives should be long and slow. Red zone is the swing factor: the Vikings have allowed touchdowns on roughly 12% of opponent red-zone trips, and Tampa Bay kicked four Chase McLaughlin field goals in a 23-19 home loss to Cleveland while managing one offensive touchdown.
- **Goal-line carries matter here.** With Jordan Mason on IR after thumb surgery, the short-yardage work Mason handled in Week 1 (including a 1-yard score) now funnels to Aaron Jones Sr., who has 35 carries in two games.

**Baltimore turned the page on an era.** Jesse Minter replaced John Harbaugh after 17 seasons, bringing his Michigan and Chargers defensive background with him, and the front office paid up for edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, who logged his first sack as a Raven in Week 2. The offensive core is unchanged and still built around Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry, with rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane already lost to a wrist injury and on IR.
- **Dallas spent on the interior and the perimeter.** Quinnen Williams headlines the defensive line rebuild, Jaishawn Barham adds young legs at linebacker, and George Pickens is now a full-season complement to CeeDee Lamb rather than a rental.
- Javonte Williams is the clear lead back with Emari Demercado, Tyler Goodson and fullback Hunter Luepke behind him.
- Brian Schottenheimer's second year has produced a top-10 scoring offense (28.5 points per game) and a defense that has not held up.
sections.matchup:
**This is a pace-and-efficiency mismatch pointed at the Cowboys defense.** Dallas is 29th in opponent EPA per play and 31st in opponent success rate, has generated only two sacks in two games, and is 24th at 5.8 opponent yards per play — and Baltimore leads the league at 6.8 yards per play. On the ground Dallas ranks 28th in rush EPA per play and has surrendered 347 rushing yards at 5.0 per carry, which is the single cleanest path to Derrick Henry's fifth and sixth touchdowns of the year behind Baltimore's 29.5 rushing attempts per game (9th).
- **Dallas's counter is red-zone conversion, not volume.** The Cowboys are 2nd in the NFL at 85.7% red-zone scoring on 3.5 trips per game, but they are 31st in rushing attempts per game (19.5), so Javonte Williams's touchdown equity is goal-line-share dependent rather than carry-volume dependent.
- **Baltimore's defense is stout in front and soft behind.** The Ravens are 6th at 4.7 opponent yards per play and held New Orleans's backs to a handful of fantasy points, but they rank 27th against the pass (559 yards allowed) and 26th in opponent red-zone scoring at 80%.
- With Dallas down three defensive backs, expect more soft zone and more Lamar Jackson designed-keep and scramble equity inside the 10; with Baltimore's coverage leaking, Dak Prescott's tight end and slot targets are the live counterpunch.
sections.injuries:
**Dallas's secondary is the story.** Safety Malik Hooker (forearm fracture) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) were already inactive in Week 2, and the Commanders win cost them cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring, Schottenheimer said "a few weeks") and safety P.J. Locke, who tore the plantar fascia in his foot and left in a walking boot. Ten Cowboys were limited in the first post-game session, including guard Tyler Booker (ankle), defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (neck), receiver KaVontae Turpin (shoulder) and running back Javonte Williams (neck); tight end Jake Ferguson cleared a concussion check and finished Week 2 with two touchdowns.
- **Baltimore is closer to whole.** Zay Flowers missed the Saints game with a hamstring after being downgraded to doubtful, but he practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and Minter said he has a "good shot" for Rio — books have posted a full, normal-looking prop menu for him, which is the strongest tell available.
- Left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe) and guard John Simpson (groin) both missed practice time and still played, and Trey Hendrickson (finger) played through it.
- Defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) has still not debuted, and rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is on IR.

**The headline is the reunion.** Klint Kubiak, the Saints' offensive coordinator in 2024 before a Super Bowl-winning season as Seattle's OC in 2025, walks into the Superdome as Las Vegas' first-year head coach, and edge rusher Tyree Wilson was traded from the Raiders to New Orleans during the 2026 draft.
- **Las Vegas spent big on the passing game:** Kirk Cousins signed for five years and $172M, Jalen Nailor for three years and $35M, plus Tyler Linderbaum at center, Kwity Paye and Nakobe Dean on defense, with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza sitting behind Cousins.
- **New Orleans is in year two under Kellen Moore**, having handed the offense to Tyler Shough and added Travis Etienne Jr. (four years, $52M), TE Noah Fant and G David Edwards while losing Demario Davis.
The Raiders are 2-0 after beating Miami 27-13 and the Chargers 26-14; the Saints are 1-1, losing 31-30 in overtime at Detroit after a 21-0 comeback and winning 24-17 at Baltimore. Both teams have outperformed summer expectations, but the schedules behind those records look very different.
sections.matchup:
**New Orleans has been the more productive offense and the leakier defense.** The Saints average 409 total yards (331 passing) at the league's fastest offensive pace, while the Raiders sit at 300 yards per game with only 93.5 on the ground.
- **The Saints' run defense is the soft spot:** 136.5 rushing yards allowed per game and the sixth-most fantasy points surrendered to running backs through two weeks, which points straight at Ashton Jeanty, who played 81% of snaps and saw 28 intended touches in Week 2.
- **Las Vegas' 13.5 points allowed per game is schedule-inflated**, built against Miami and a Chargers offense with a thin receiving corps, though Kwity Paye already has two sacks and the front generated five in the opener.
- **Saints touchdown equity is concentrated**, with Chris Olave at 18 catches for 268 yards and Shough keeping the ball himself on the goal line for the game-winner in Baltimore.
New Orleans' backfield split (Etienne Jr. 17 carries, Alvin Kamara nine) muddies the goal-line picture, so the cleanest red-zone reads are Olave outside and the tight ends working the seam.
sections.injuries:
**Brock Bowers is the swing piece.** The Raiders tight end had a meniscus trim just before the season, missed both games, returned to limited practice late in Week 2 and worked out pregame; Kubiak called him "very close," and he is listed questionable heading into Week 3.
- **Las Vegas also carries** CB Darien Porter (foot), S Treydan Stukes (concussion), WR Dareke Young (hamstring) and QB Aidan O'Connell (personal) as questionable, with Justin Shorter placed on injured reserve.
- **New Orleans is without LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle)**, who left the Ravens game in the fourth quarter, and lists CB Martin Emerson Jr. (shoulder), DT Christen Miller (toe), LB Isaiah Stalbird (shoulder) and RB Audric Estime (thigh) as questionable.

Wednesday and Thursday practice reports will settle Bowers and Banks Jr.; both meaningfully move the touchdown board.

sections.offseason:
- Both teams reshaped their front sevens and receiver rooms, and both arrive at 1-1 after a blowout loss followed by a comfortable win.
- The **Rams** made the loudest defensive moves, adding **Myles Garrett** and welcoming **Aaron Donald** back from retirement, though Garrett is already on injured reserve with a knee issue and Donald is being managed on a snap count.
- Los Angeles opened with a 27-7 home loss to San Francisco in which Matthew Stafford threw for just 155 yards, then answered with a 28-6 win over the Giants on Monday night behind a 327-yard, four-touchdown night.
- **Denver** traded a first, a third and a fourth to Miami for **Jaylen Waddle**, pairing him with Courtland Sutton, and drafted running back Jonah Coleman, who has already forced his way into the rotation.
- The Broncos were beaten 31-10 at Kansas City in Week 1 with Bo Nix sacked four times, then rallied from 13-3 down to beat Jacksonville 20-13 at home.
- Sean Payton's group has scored three touchdowns in two games; Sean McVay's has five.
sections.matchup:
- The cleanest edge on the board is the **Rams' ground game against Denver's run defense**, which has allowed 157.5 rushing yards per game, roughly 5.1 yards per carry, and rates dead last in EPA allowed per rush.
- Los Angeles runs a genuine committee with **Kyren Williams** (23 carries) and **Blake Corum** (22 carries) nearly even, but Williams owns the short-yardage and goal-line work and has both of the backfield's scores, including a 5-yard rush in Week 1 and a 10-yard receiving touchdown in Week 2.
- Denver's counter is its secondary: **Patrick Surtain II** and Riley Moss have held opponents to 186.5 passing yards per game, and Surtain is the reason Davante Adams' 195-yard Monday night will be very hard to repeat.
- The Broncos' offense is the problem in this game, converting only 26.1 percent of third downs and just 42.9 percent of red-zone trips into touchdowns, with one first-half drive stalling at the 1-yard line and another ending in an interception at the 8.
- Denver has funneled its red-zone passing to tight ends, with **Evan Engram** and **Nate Adkins** accounting for two of the team's three touchdowns, while Waddle (10 targets) is the volume leader and Sutton the jump-ball option.
- The Rams have been efficient where it counts, scoring touchdowns on 80 percent of red-zone possessions, and their defense is allowing 281 total yards and 16.5 points per game.
sections.injuries:
- **Puka Nacua (WR, LAR) is questionable with a groin/hip issue** and is the single biggest swing factor; he developed soreness after Thursday practice in Week 2, sat Friday and Saturday, and was inactive against the Giants.
- Sean McVay said Tuesday, "I'm not sure what his status is as far as this next coming week. I'm hopeful that he'll play," and noted the Rams err on the side of caution with soft-tissue injuries, so Wednesday-through-Friday participation is the real tell.
- With Nacua out in Week 2, Davante Adams saw 10 targets and rookie tight end **Terrance Ferguson** saw nine and scored, a usage pattern worth tracking if Nacua sits again.
- Denver's backfield is a mess: **J.K. Dobbins** and **RJ Harvey** are both questionable with hamstrings, Harvey already missed Week 2, and Payton has said only that both have a chance to play.
- **Marvin Mims Jr.** is questionable with a foot injury, guard Nick Gargiulo is out with a torn ACL, and linebacker Jonathon Cooper is out for personal reasons.
- The Rams have also lost **Myles Garrett** to injured reserve after arthroscopic knee surgery, with Jordan Whittington (quadriceps), Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) and Ronnie Rivers (calf) all questionable.
sections.oddsNotes:
- DraftKings has the Rams as a **road favourite at -2.5** with a total of 45.5, and the moneyline quoted for this card is LAR -142 / DEN +120, which de-vigs to roughly 56.3 percent Los Angeles.
- The market has drifted toward the Rams since the opener; ESPN's DraftKings feed still shows LAR -135 / DEN +114, and Covers had the total as low as 44.5 earlier in the week before BetMGM and DraftKings settled on 45.5.
- ESPN's matchup predictor is well ahead of the market at 63.8 percent for Los Angeles, which is a gap worth noting but not one I would fully trust given the Nacua uncertainty and the altitude.
- The derived team totals are **Rams 24.0 and Broncos 21.5**, and the total-touchdowns market backs that up with over 4.5 priced at -166 on DraftKings and over 5.5 at +120.
- Public-facing analysts at Covers, Sportsbook Review and BettorsInsider have all landed on the Under, so there is no contrarian edge left on that side, only a reasoned one.
sections.atdNotes:
- Anytime touchdown boards are posted at **DraftKings, FanDuel, Caesars and bet365**; BetMGM had game props up but no anytime scorer market in the feed I checked, so every price below is attributed to a book that actually posted it.
- **bet365 is systematically longer on Rams skill players** than the rest of the market - Ferguson +375 versus +255 elsewhere, Corum +375 versus +270, Adams +150 versus +115 - which makes it the place to shop the Los Angeles side.
- **Puka Nacua is priced at +125 to +129 with no visible injury discount**, which reads as the market assuming he plays; even a fully healthy Nacua has never been a high-rate touchdown scorer, and he has none through Week 1, so that number does not pay for the availability risk.
- The **Denver backfield prices do not add up**: Dobbins +120, Coleman +135 and Harvey +230 sum to well over a full touchdown of probability for a committee that should produce roughly one rushing score, with two of the three carrying hamstrings.
- Notably, **no receiving-yards prop is posted for Adams or Nacua** at any of the four books, while Waddle has a full board at 57.5 yards, another sign the Rams receiver market is being held pending Wednesday's practice report.

sections.offseason:
**Philadelphia reshaped its skill group and its offensive staff.** A.J. Brown was traded to New England, Sean Mannion was installed as offensive coordinator on 29 January 2026, and long-time offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland departed after 13 seasons. The Eagles added WR Marquise Brown, CB Riq Woolen, OLB Jonathan Greenard on a four-year deal and RB Tank Bigsby via trade, while Vic Fangio stayed on as defensive coordinator.
- **Chicago** is in year two of Ben Johnson's rebuild, with Press Taylor listed as offensive coordinator and Dennis Allen running the defense.
- The Bears' skill group is young: Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and TE Colston Loveland alongside veteran Cole Kmet.
- The two-back committee of D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai has been the clearest identity marker of the new Chicago offense.
sections.matchup:
**This is a low-variance, run-first script against two defenses that have already shown teeth.** Chicago scored 59 on Carolina with six rushing touchdowns and went 4-for-4 in the red zone, then reached the Minnesota red zone three times in Week 2 and came away with zero points, including a D'Andre Swift fumble on first-and-goal from the one. The Bears' yards per play collapsed from 7.9 to 4.2 and they surrendered four sacks, which is the number that matters most against a Fangio front that can rush four and play two-high.
- **Philadelphia's offense has not matched its record**: 27th in success rate and 24th in first downs per game while winning 24-22 and 24-20.
- Eagles backs averaged under three yards per carry in Tennessee behind a reshuffled line with Drew Kendall at center and Cam Jurgens at left guard.
- With Dallas Goedert out, Philadelphia's red-zone and end-zone work concentrates on DeVonta Smith and on Jalen Hurts' own goal-line sneak package.
- Chicago's counter is Swift and Monangai on early downs to keep a compromised quarterback out of obvious passing situations.
sections.injuries:
**The Bears' quarterback room is the story of the week.** Caleb Williams strained his right hamstring scrambling in the fourth quarter against Minnesota, is officially week-to-week, is not expected to practice, and has not been formally ruled out by Ben Johnson. Backup Tyson Bagent, who relieved him and went 5-of-9 for 54 yards, entered concussion protocol after a Dallas Turner sack, and 38-year-old Case Keenum, whose last regular-season start came in 2023 with Houston, is the emergency option; the Monday kickoff buys Chicago an extra day of protocol time.
- **Dallas Goedert** sprained his MCL run blocking and is expected to miss a few weeks; Philadelphia signed Zach Ertz to the practice squad and can elevate him for this game.
- **Saquon Barkley** took a stinger on the opening drive, missed the first half, returned for four carries and nine yards, and had imaging done on the shoulder.
- Jalen Carter's late exit was a calf cramp and he is expected to be fine; the Eagles' pass rush was noticeably flat without Jonathan Greenard, and Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve.
sections.oddsNotes:
**The market has moved six points on the spread and five on the total since the look-ahead.** Chicago was posted as a 1.5-point home favorite with a 46.5 total before Week 2; it now sits at PHI -4.5 with a 41.5 total across DraftKings, FanDuel, Caesars, bet365 and Fanatics, with BetMGM and BetRivers holding 42. Moneylines are tightly clustered at PHI -215 to -225 and CHI +175 to +185, so the -218/+180 quote is on the fair side of the range.
- De-vigged, that is roughly **65.7% Philadelphia / 34.3% Chicago**.
- Implied team totals from the spread and total are 23.0 for road favorite Philadelphia and 18.5 for Chicago.
- Juice sits slightly on the Over (-112 to -117) at most books, which is mild resistance to further downward movement.

Buffalo is 2-0 averaging 38.5 points and 7.1 yards per play while the Chargers sit 28th in points per drive and have scored exactly 14 in each loss. The personnel gap is concrete this week: Los Angeles has both starting tight ends on IR, its starting left guard and starting defensive tackle expected out, and Derwin James Jr. in a cast, all on a 10am body-clock road trip against a Bills team on extra rest that led the NFL with 14 pressures in Week 2 against an offensive line that put the ball on the ground six times. I make it Bills by nine with the total landing just above the number.

Carolina holds a clear efficiency and volume edge: 6.7 yards per play and 61 snaps a game against a Cleveland offence at 16.5 points, 52 snaps and the worst yards before contact in the NFL. That gap justifies laying a short road number even with Carolina's 28th-ranked defence and a patched offensive line. The total is the softer side: Cleveland's pace and red-zone problems argue under, but Carolina has hung 71 points in two weeks. A 24-20 projection sits just under the number, so the under is a lean rather than a conviction play.

Kansas City is clearly the better team, but 11.5 is a price rather than a projection and this specific Chiefs team converts yards into field goals — Harrison Butker kicked five of them in Week 2 on 523 yards of offense, and Kansas City is 2-8 against the spread over its last 10 games. A 1:00 PM ET kickoff in Miami Gardens in late September is a genuine fatigue variable for a visiting team, and Miami's only two offensive touchdowns this year have both been chunk plays, which is exactly the shape of a late backdoor cover.
